title: Kill switches, tested
description:
Three switches, each one operation and each with a test that proves it stops work before the next run or send: pause one agent; pause every agent on a site; pause sending on one channel account (the existing announcement pause). A pause is checked by the runner at the start of a run and by the sender at the start of an attempt. Resuming never replays skipped ticks; waiting records keep their due times. For an agent woken only by changes, resume sends one wake per subject that changed during the pause, found by index from the subject's own updated time, never by walking a table; the wake keys make repeats harmless.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Each switch stops the next run or attempt.
- A paused send is recorded as waiting, not failed.
- Resuming does not flood, and work that arrived during the pause is picked up once.
- Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs (below).

**Gherkin features needed**
- kill-switches.feature: pausing an agent stops its next run; pausing the site stops all; pausing a channel stops the next attempt; resume runs only what is still due.

**Infrastructure as code touched:** None.

**Part of:** Observability, safety and release readiness. Slice code J2 in `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md` (section 12).
**Standing rules:** no fallbacks, no workarounds, no interim systems, no arbitrary caps; no text in DynamoDB; indexes over scans; no AppSync subscriptions; nothing created by hand in AWS; no real email addresses in specs or fixtures; status shown as words and marks, never colour alone.

comments.text: Merged to develop in #1882: resume sends each subject's latest stopped change wake once (no ticks, no duplicates); features_backend/agents/kill-switches.feature. Closes on release.
